question.text: The Subscription Agreement for Nirmala Opportunities Fund contains representations and warranties by the investor. Which of the following is a standard investor representation?

answer.text: The investor guarantees a minimum return from the fund
The investor warrants that the fund manager will act in good faith
The investor confirms that they are an eligible investor as defined under SEBI AIF Regulations and that the investment funds are from legitimate sources
The investor represents that SEBI has approved the fund's investment strategy

explanation.text: The Logic: The XIX-A workbook supports that the Contribution Agreement / Subscription Agreement contains contributor-specific representations and warranties; investor eligibility checks; FATCA notes; KYC and AML/CFT documentation cooperation; and source-of-funds-related fraud controls. Confirming eligible-investor status under the SEBI AIF Regulations and confirming legitimate source of funds are therefore standard investor representations supported by the workbook. The Trap: Funds do not guarantee returns; investors do not warrant the manager's conduct (that flows the other way); and SEBI does not approve specific investment strategies, so investors cannot represent any such approval. Note: The XIX-A workbook does not enumerate every "standard" investor representation by name; the eligibility + legitimate-source-of-funds answer aligns with the SEBI AIF Regulations + AML framework the workbook references.
